description: Wikipedia search about Welsh and Irish immigrant coal miners in 19th century Pennsylvania

response.title: Anthracite coal region
response.extract: The anthracite coal region of northeastern Pennsylvania drew successive waves of immigrant miners during the 19th century. Welsh miners, experienced in hard-coal techniques from South Wales, were among the earliest arrivals in the 1820s–1840s and held supervisory positions. Irish immigrants, many fleeing the Great Famine of the 1840s, filled unskilled and semi-skilled roles. By the 1870s–1880s, Southern and Eastern European immigrants — Poles, Lithuanians, Slovaks, and Ukrainians — transformed the workforce again. Each wave brought distinct religious institutions, fraternal organizations, and burial societies that generated genealogical records.
